description: The Farkas acceptor component: check(system: list<ineq>, y: list<s64>) -> bool with record ineq { coeffs: list<tuple<u32, s64>>, bound: s64 }. Expected outcomes follow Silmaril.Logic.LinArith.Carrier.farkasCheck within the module's bounds (|y|, |b|, |a| <= 2^30, y >= 0, variables < 8192, accumulators within 2^62); outside them the module rejects valid certificates (sound but incomplete), noted per case.

claims.scope: Every reference Component Model reading of what the bytes parse to (Silmaril.Wasm.Examples.FarkasAccept.bytes, regenerated as examples/wasm-acceptors/farkas_accept.wasm): an accepting call implies that the system is infeasible. Soundness only: nothing is stated about rejections, traps or completeness (the checker is bounded).

theorems.states: check returns true on S, y ⇒ S ∈ Infeasible

farkas.source: Silmaril.Wasm.Examples.FarkasAccept: prog, wrapped as a component (memory 0 = core memory 1, realloc cabi_realloc)

cases.name: two-row
cases.note: x0 <= 1, -x0 <= -2 with y = [1, 1]; LinArith.sys₁_infeasible_rat

cases.name: three-row
cases.note: x0 + x1 <= 2, -x0 <= -1, -x1 <= -2 with y = [1, 1, 1]; LinArith.sys₂_infeasible

cases.name: empty-row
cases.note: 0 <= -1 alone

cases.name: zero-multiplier-extra-row
cases.note: two-row plus a row with multiplier 0

cases.name: repeated-variable
cases.note: x0 + x0 <= 1, -2 x0 <= -3: repeated variables add up

cases.name: repeated-variable-cancel
cases.note: x3 - x3 <= -1 in one row

cases.name: order-of-coefficients
cases.note: three-row with the first row's pairs swapped

cases.name: chain-301
cases.note: x_i - x_{i+1} <= 0 (i < 300), x_300 - x_0 <= -1, all multipliers 1

cases.name: variable-8191
cases.note: the largest variable index within the module's bound (j < 8192)

cases.name: coefficient-2^30
cases.note: coefficients +-2^30, at the module's bound

cases.name: multiplier-2^30
cases.note: multipliers 2^30, at the module's bound

cases.name: bound-minus-2^30
cases.note: bound -2^30, at the module's bound

cases.name: feasible
cases.note: x0 <= 1, -x0 <= 0 is feasible; the weighted bounds add up to 1

cases.name: feasible-zero-multipliers
cases.note: all multipliers 0: the bound sum 0 is not negative

cases.name: negative-multiplier
cases.note: 0 <= 1 (feasible) with y = [-1]: the bound sum would be -1

cases.name: negative-multiplier-two
cases.note: x0 <= 1, x0 <= 2 (feasible) with y = [-1, 1]

cases.name: wrong-multipliers
cases.note: y = [1, 2]: the left-hand sides do not cancel

cases.name: too-few-multipliers
cases.note: one multiplier for two inequalities (yl != sl)

cases.name: too-many-multipliers
cases.note: three multipliers for two inequalities (yl != sl)

cases.name: empty-system
cases.note: no inequality: the bound sum 0 is not negative

cases.name: empty-system-extra-multiplier
cases.note: yl != sl

cases.name: coefficient-2^30+1
cases.note: a valid certificate, rejected: |a| > 2^30 is outside the module's bound (sound but incomplete)

cases.name: multiplier-2^30+1
cases.note: a valid certificate, rejected: y > 2^30 is outside the module's bound (sound but incomplete)

cases.name: bound-minus-2^30-1
cases.note: a valid certificate, rejected: |b| > 2^30 is outside the module's bound (sound but incomplete)

cases.name: bound-s64-min
cases.note: a valid certificate, rejected: bound -2^63 is outside the module's bound

cases.name: variable-8192
cases.note: a valid certificate, rejected: variable index j >= 8192 is outside the module's bound (sound but incomplete)

cases.name: variable-u32-max
cases.note: a valid certificate, rejected: j = 2^32 - 1 >= 8192

cases.name: variable-alias-8192
cases.note: x0 <= 1, -x8192 <= -2 is feasible; slot 8192 mod 8192 = 0 would cancel x0, but j >= 8192 sets the flag

cases.name: overflow-wrap
cases.note: y a = 2^64 wraps to 0 in i64 and 2^32 x0 <= -1 is feasible; out of the bounds, rejected
